Hi Sara,

Really helpful context — thanks for the profile. Quick summary and next steps below:

Summary (high-level):
- H100-80GB will give the best perf for the long-context summarization (lower latency at large sequence lengths) but comes at a premium.
- A100-80GB is a good balance for mixed workloads and tends to be the most cost-effective for sustained throughput if you don't need the latest tensor core features.
- L40S-48GB is the best perf/$ for throughput-only lanes (embedding & NER) but doesn't handle 32k contexts well.

Commercial suggestions:
- Initial reserved commit: 24 GPUs (mix: 12 H100 / 8 A100 / 4 L40S) to balance memory and throughput. This supports ~100 sustained qps with autoscaling headroom for bursts to ~350–450 qps depending on batching.
- Commit term options: 12-month (flexible, lower discount), 24-month (balanced), 36-month (max discount). Typical discounts: ~15% (12m), ~20% (24m), ~28% (36m) off list for sizable commitments — I'll confirm exact phrasing with pricing ops.
- SLOs: we can target 99.9% availability and provide throughput guarantees per-route. Latency p95 will depend on batching; expect p95 ~120–250ms for generation at 8k tokens on H100 with optimized kernels (A100 ~160–320ms depending on load).

I'll loop in Aditya (SE) and Dev (sales ops) to validate perf/$ numbers and build a formal quote. Can you do a 30-min call Tues 10/5 or Wed 10/6?

I'll attach a one-page options recap.

Kimberly / team,

I ran the workload profile against our benchmark suite and the quick conclusions:

Perf/$ (rough, normalized to tokens/sec per $1/hr):
- H100-80GB: best raw throughput for long sequences (~1.0x baseline) and best tail latency for 8k–32k; cost premium ~+35% vs A100 list.
- A100-80GB: ~0.78x baseline for very long contexts but ~15–20% cheaper per hour vs H100 in many regions — the sweet spot for mixed workloads.
- L40S-48GB: ~0.6x on long-context ops but ~0.55x cost vs A100 (i.e., cheaper), making it ideal for throughput-only lanes.

Concrete recommendation for Aurora (to hit their targets):
- Hybrid pool: 10 H100, 8 A100, 6 L40S (total 24 reserved). Rationale: keep H100s dedicated to 8k+ summarization jobs, A100s for general generations, L40S for embedding/NER batch work.
- Autoscale + burst: configure burst capacity to allow +60% GPU burst across the pool on peak hours (pay-as-you-go pricing for burst). This supports daytime bursts up to ~420–480 QPS depending on batching.

Estimated latency (p95, with optimized kernels & continuous batching where applicable):
- 4k tokens: H100 ~90–120ms, A100 ~120–160ms, L40S not recommended for 4k+ generation.
- 8k tokens: H100 ~130–180ms, A100 ~180–250ms.
- 32k tokens: H100 ~350–600ms (depends heavily on micro-batching); A100 may exceed 1s or require splitting sequences.

Pricing sketch (list per GPU / month equivalence, region: us-west):
- H100-80GB list: $13.50/hr (~$9,900/mo equivalent)
- A100-80GB list: $10.00/hr (~$7,320/mo equivalent)
- L40S-48GB list: $5.50/hr (~$4,026/mo equivalent)

Discount guidance and commit structures:
- 12-month: recommend 15% off list for this mix.
- 24-month: 20% off list.
- 36-month: 28% off list + potential for fixed-price escalator clauses.

Commercial math example (24 GPU commit, 12m):
- Effective monthly cost (list, blended): ~$(24 * blended_rate * 24*30) — I'll attach a workbook with the exact math.

Attachments: aurora_sizing_model_v2.xlsx (contains per-hour/day/month breaks and burst scenarios).

If we want to be aggressive on win velocity, I can support a limited 18% discount on 12m under AE signoff + RevOps approval; higher discounts need manager approval. Hannah, please advise if 18% is OK for this stage.
